description:
What is unclear and for whom: a contributor writing pkix-aia-http or a third-party adapter will naturally reach for '?' on a std::io::Error result. The current pkix-aia surface forces manual decomposition into AiaError::IoFailure { kind: e.kind(), message: e.to_string() }. A reader of pkix-aia/src/lib.rs/AiaError will not immediately see why From<std::io::Error> was excluded.

The reason (recorded only by inference): std::io::Error is not Clone + PartialEq + Eq + Serialize, so embedding it directly would block AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6. Decomposing into IoFailure { kind, message } is the workaround. But a From impl that performs the decomposition COULD exist — it would just be a lossy conversion (os_error() numeric code is dropped per existing doc at lines 192-195).

What would make it clear: add a rustdoc comment block (just below the IoFailure variant or at the end of impl AiaError section) explaining:

'No impl From<std::io::Error> for AiaError exists. Adapters MUST construct IoFailure explicitly with the relevant fields. Rationale: std::io::Error embeds a raw OS errno that would silently drop in the From impl. Forcing explicit construction makes the loss of information visible at every conversion site. Adapters that want a one-liner conversion can implement a private helper in their own crate.'

This trips one of the AGENTS.md preferences (record decisions a future contributor would otherwise re-litigate). Not a code defect.
title: No From<std::io::Error> impl on AiaError; rationale only implicit
